author: gpt-5.6-luna
kind: a program folder for a mobile app re-platform: roadmap.md, a ticket export (JSON, 150 to 220 tickets), a vendor contract summary with dates, an org chart with owners and a meeting-notes folder (6 to 10 short notes)
scenario: A director asks: what could stop us shipping in September, and who owns each one? I need this for the steering review.
seeds: (1) a single person is the only assignee on every ticket of one critical component (key-person risk); (2) the vendor contract notes an API deprecation date that falls before the launch; (3) an unowned ticket on the critical chain; (4) scope creep: a meeting note quietly adds a requirement that has no ticket yet; (5) a code freeze in the roadmap that collides with a public holiday week; (6) a decoy: a scary-sounding risk in one meeting note that a later note says is resolved.
shape: {"risks": [{"id": str, "tickets": [ids], "kind": "key-person|vendor|unowned|scope|schedule|other", "likelihood": "low|medium|high", "impact": "low|medium|high", "owner": str, "mitigation": str, "trigger_date": "YYYY-MM-DD or null"}], "top_three": [risk ids]}
expertSources: Site Reliability Engineering (book), Release Engineering, https://sre.google/sre-book/release-engineering/ (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, idea only)
